core_rule.rule: When seeking a specific henchman, use normal henchman hiring rules except as modified here.
Likelihood of finding desired henchmen varies by market class.
Class rarity values are baseline suggestions for an average human settlement and may be adjusted by the Judge for location or campaign conditions.

procedure.name: find_henchman_of_specific_class
procedure.step: Determine that class's rarity from the applicable class-rarity table, subject to Judge adjustment.
Consult the henchman class availability by market class table for the current market class.
Roll for availability once per month for each desired class.
Limit successful results by the total number of henchmen the market can support using normal henchman availability for that market.
After one month, new henchmen arrive and the search may be attempted again.

procedure.name: determine_henchman_level_after_successful_hire
procedure.step: Roll 1d20 on the random henchman level table.
If hiring in a Class VI market, apply a -2 penalty to the roll.
Read the resulting level from the table.

commissioning.rule: Characters may commission the hire of a henchman in the same way equipment may be commissioned.
The character must let it be known that a specific henchman is sought and must be willing to wait to hire them.
The character must pay the Searching for Henchmen fee by market class for a full month.
After paying the fee for the month, the character rolls for availability as though the desired class were one rarity lower.
If the search fails, the character may continue searching and roll again each month.

general_proficiency_search.rule: Finding a henchman with one rank in a specific general proficiency is Common rarity.
Finding a henchman with two ranks in a specific general proficiency is Uncommon rarity.
Finding a henchman with three ranks in a specific general proficiency is Rare rarity.
If such a henchman is found, generate the henchman's class as normal for a henchman found in that location.

class_or_combination_search.rule: For a class proficiency, or for a specific class combined with a specific general proficiency, begin with the rarity of the specific class.
If multiple classes can have the desired proficiency and the hiring character does not care which class is found, use the lowest applicable class rarity.
Increase rarity by one step for each rank in the desired proficiency or proficiencies.
If the modified rarity would exceed Legendary, the henchman cannot be found by this method.
When the method cannot produce the desired result, the hiring character must accept whatever is found, which may or may not match the request.

seeking_specific_class_and_level.rule: To seek a henchman of a specific class and level, choose the desired class and level first.
Seeking a level 1 henchman applies no rarity modifier.
For each level above 1, increase rarity by one step.
If modified rarity would exceed Legendary, the henchman cannot be found by this method.
When the method cannot produce the desired result, the hiring character must accept whatever is found, which may or may not match the request.

procedure.name: evaluate_class_rarity
procedure.step: Apply the listed modifiers for class traits.
Cap the result at Legendary unless the Judge instead rules the class unavailable for hire.

modifier.condition: for each kind of magic the class can cast
class has exceptional abilities not otherwise covered
class is an extremely specialized subset of a core class
class has exceptional ability score requirements

definitions.definition: For these guidelines, core means appears in ACKS Core; this definition may vary by campaign.

rarity_evaluation_guidelines.rule: These are baseline guidelines only; listed class rarities need not exactly match the guideline result in every case.
If a computed rarity would exceed Legendary, the Judge may either treat it as Legendary or declare the class unavailable for hire.

source_notes.rule: In the standard campaign class-rarity table, classes printed in italics are from Player's Companion.
In the Heroic Fantasy class-rarity table, classes printed in italics are from Player's Companion and classes printed in bold italics are from Heroic Fantasy Handbook.

notes_to_build_agent.note: The Heroic Fantasy classes, and several other classes, are not included for v1 of the app, but appear in these tables for completeness.
Build the systems that rely on these tables to be adjustable depending on which classes are included in a campaign, and to be adjustable for new, custom, or later-added classes.
